parsed.explanation: Combined operative regime is High-to-Elevated risk. Entry: a national cable refuses applicants with document or record discrepancies and allows a lifetime fraud ineligibility finding; passports are restricted to M/F, and home-issued documents can be blocked. Facilities: bans on birth-sex facilities cover government buildings in roughly 10 states, with some private-setting reach in 6 and criminal trespass exposure in 4. The division's own order backs single-sex facilities, and a 2022 case documents birth-sex prison housing followed by sexual assault with no remedy. Custody harm is documented nationally (forced labour, beatings, and a 2026 conversion-therapy policy). The division has no statewide gender-identity hate or discrimination statute, but national law covers hate crimes, employment, and housing, and marriage recognition is settled. Repeated record-based findings show the exposures are unremedied.

entry_documents.exposure: National cable refuses applicants with document discrepancies and permits lifetime fraud ineligibility; passports restricted to M/F, with reported confiscations and strandings.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; litigation pending with no operative relief documented for visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Home-passport mismatch triggers refusal at entry; the fraud ground can convert a mismatch into permanent exclusion.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented trespass arrest in a state capitol restroom (handcuffed, 24 hours held in men's ward). Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary, and sexual abuse. Birth-sex prison housing in the division with a failure-to-protect ruling for the state.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Pretrial release was available; the trespass offence requires willful entry plus refusal to leave, not automatic arrest.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document or facility friction can move into local detention, which then places the person by birth sex with no working remedy.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal government facilities restricted by EO. Government-building facility bans in about 10 states, school/government bans in 9 more, and some private-setting reach in 6. Division EO backs single-sex bathrooms and changing rooms.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No state-wide facility mandate is recorded for private venues in the division; 29 states have no mapped ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility rules apply to government buildings a visitor enters, and state-law definitions may reach access beyond the mapped laws.

care_services.exposure: Under-19 gender-affirming care is banned in the division and upheld. A visitor cannot obtain it for a minor in their care. National subpoenas of hospital records and proposed rules barring insurance reimbursement for under-18 care.
care_services.protection: Adult care access is not recorded as barred in the division; no adult-care barrier is documented.
care_services.interaction: A minor needing care meets a hard local bar; a hospital encounter can expose records to federal process.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National EO calls gender-affirming care 'mutilation'; directs investigation and prosecution of teachers using preferred names; the May 2026 counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for neutralisation; the division EO frames gender identity as not recognised.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The counterterrorism strategy disclaims targeting people who merely disagree; several orders are enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State-level framing and federal security framing reinforce each other, raising the chance that an encounter is treated as a threat.

minors_guardians.exposure: A visitor under 19 cannot obtain gender-affirming care in the division; a guardian cannot obtain it for a minor in their care. Athletics ban for trans students; school-based federal enforcement threats.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented for minors beyond the marriage and adoption recognition noted in the division.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor is subject to facility, care, and school rules; a parent accompanying the minor meets the same bars.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific homicide or assault rate is sourced. Anti-bias coverage is partial: the division has no gender-identity hate statute; national law covers hate crimes; 37 states lacked state-level anti-bias statutes as of 2019.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime charging is available for gender-identity crimes; a 2016 state ruling shows the state statute applies to perceived-association bias.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A bias crime in the division can be charged federally, but local police response data is absent.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: The division has no state-wide discrimination statute. Remedies for facility, custody, and document harms are documented as failing or unremedied, and the prison ruling found no remedy.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National employment (2020) and housing (2021) protections operate; one city ordinance covers employment and accommodation; marriage recognition is settled; sodomy statute repealed.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists for discrimination but not for facility, custody, or entry exposures, which are the main traveller-facing harms.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: both use a universal rule with documented exclusion and no effective remedy. This case adds custody harm and a lifetime fraud ground, but lacks a formal visitor exclusion register and an airline verification mandate, so it sits at about the same level.

Similar: both house by birth sex with documented assaults, and both criminalise presentation in government buildings. This case adds immigration-custody forced labour and national entry screening, which pushes it lower, but it has marriage recognition and national anti-discrimination law, which pushes it slightly higher.

Higher: the 0.45 anchor shows registration and exposure, but imprisonment and custody harm are not documented at the level seen here. This case has documented birth-sex custody and a criminal trespass arrest, so it sits lower.

Higher: the 0.55 anchor involves administrative refusal and secondary screening without documented custody violence or birth-sex placement. This case has documented custody harm and a criminal arrest, so it sits lower.

parsed.synthesis: Traveller-facing exposures stack across sovereigns. A home-passport mismatch can trigger refusal and a lifetime fraud finding at entry. A government-building facility or restroom encounter can lead to trespass arrest and detention, and state custody then places the person by birth sex with documented assault and no working remedy. Federal custody adds documented abuse. A visiting minor or guardian meets the under-19 care bar. National protections on employment, housing, hate crime, and marriage are real but do not reach facility, entry, or custody exposures. The record shows recurring state-enforced exposures without a working remedy, which places the combined regime in the high-to-elevated band.
